articles.headline: Travis Etienne logs limited practice
keyFacts: New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne was a limited practice participant on Thursday, November 12, due to a hamstring injury.
Reporter Ross Jackson stated that Etienne is heading in the right direction with back-to-back limited sessions, though he is not guaranteed to play in Week 10.
Fantasy managers are advised to monitor Etienne's status following Friday's practice before deciding to start him as a running back option.
body: New Orleans Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was a limited participant in practice Thursday, Nov. 12.
SOURCE: Ross Jackson

Why it Matters: Etienne has returned to practice with back-to-back limited sessions, so while he is heading in the right direction, he is not a lock to play in Week 10. Etienne should be a RB2 option whenever he returns, but make sure to check on his status after Friday's practice.

articles.headline: Cowboys’ Christian Parker breaks down biggest key to slowing down red-hot 49ers
keyFacts: Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker identified pre-snap motion as a major challenge when facing the San Francisco 49ers.
Parker emphasized that eye discipline and knowing opponent locations are critical to slowing down the 49ers' high-scoring offense.
The 49ers enter the Week 10 matchup averaging 29.4 points per game while relying on pre-snap movement to create mismatches.
body: Mandatory Credit: Chris Jones-Imagn Images Cowboys’ Christian Parker breaks down biggest key to slowing down red-hot 49ers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

The Dallas Cowboys have the unenviable task of trying to contain the high-flying attack of Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers in this coming Sunday’s Week 10 showdown at AT&T Stadium in Arlington.

Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker surely is looking at ways to slow down San Francisco’s offense, and one that he is particularly concerned about is the Niners’ pre-snap activities , as pointed out by Ed Werder of WFAA.

“Cowboys DC Christian Parker, when asked about the 49ers using presnap motion at the highest rate in the league, stressed the importance of eye discipline and to know where opponents are when ball actually snapped because ‘You don’t want to be chasing that rabbitt all day,’” Werder shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter.

The 49ers have one of the most prolific offenses in the league, entering Week 10 with an average of 29.4 points per game — third-best overall. They are also putting up 376.8 total yards per outing, and that’s despite dealing with numerous injuries. Brock Purdy has been as steady as they come at quarterback, coming into this showdown versus the Cowboys with a league-best 81.4 quarterback rating.

With weapons like do-it-all running back Christian McCaffrey and star tight end George Kittle, the 49ers have been quite a lot to deal. The 49ers love to find mismatches, and those pre-snap movements are key to making that happen for them.

It is going to be a big challenge for Parker to devise an effective plan against that San Francisco offense . On the season, the Cowboys are just 25th in the league with 26.2 points allowed per game and 30th with 372.7 total yards given up per outing.

articles.headline: Cubs superstar Pete Crow-Armstrong wins National League MVP unanimously, beating Shohei Ohtani
keyFacts: Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the National League MVP award unanimously for the 2026 season, the BBWAA revealed.
Crow-Armstrong surpassed pre-season favorite Shohei Ohtani due to injuries and a standout performance that included 45 home runs and 41 steals.
Shohei Ohtani finished in second place, and Brewers second baseman Brice Turang finished in third place in the voting.
body: Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong won the National League MVP award for the 2026 season unanimously, the BBWAA revealed Thursday evening.

The Baseball Writers' Association of America ballot uses two voters from each of the 15 chapters housing NL teams. Each voter submits a ballot with 10 players, ranked 1-10. A first-place vote gets a player 14 points, while second place earns nine, third place eight, etc., until a 10th-place vote earns one point. Ballots are due before the playoffs begin, as this is a regular-season award.

Though the results were unsurprising by the time the year wound down, going back to the start of the season, this marks a huge upset. Shohei Ohtani was the overwhelming favorite to win the award heading into the season and maintained favorite status through the All-Star break. A combination of his injuries and PCA's monster season turned the tide late.

Appearing in all 162 games, Crow-Armstrong hit .280/.372/.570 (156 OPS+) with 31 doubles, eight triples, 45 home runs, 107 RBI, 119 runs, 41 steals and 9.8 WAR. He led the majors in WAR, runs, home runs and total bases while leading the NL in slugging, OPS and OPS+. He became the (40 home runs and 40 steals in the same season). Further, he led the majors in multiple advanced defensive metrics, putting together one of the great all-around seasons from a position player in recent memory.
PCA joins the following list of Cubs to win MVP:
- Kris Bryant, 2016
- Sammy Sosa, 1998
- Andre Dawson, 1987
- Ryne Sandberg, 1984
- Ernie Banks, 1958 and 1959
- Hank Sauer, 1952
- Phil Cavaretta, 1945
- Gabby Hartnett, 1935
- Hack Wilson, 1930
- Rogers Hornsby, 1929
- Frank Schulte, 1911

Ohtani, the four-time MVP, finishes in second. At the plate, Ohtani hit .275/.377/.512 with 26 doubles, four triples, 30 home runs, 81 RBI, 89 runs, 11 steals and 3.2 WAR. On the mound, he was 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 95 strikeouts in 85 ⅔ innings with 3.2 WAR.

The nationally underrated Brewers second baseman Brice Turang finishes in third. He still hasn't made an All-Star Game, though he did start 2026 as a member of Team USA in the World Baseball Classic. In the regular season, Turang hit .268/.366/.450 (124 OPS+) with 37 doubles, three triples, 21 home runs, 100 RBI, 102 runs and 7.3 WAR, rating out as one of the best defenders in baseball.

articles.headline: Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong and Astros’ Yordan Alvarez unanimously win MVP awards
keyFacts: Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez unanimously won the National League and American League MVP awards on Thursday.
Crow-Armstrong batted .280 with 45 home runs, 107 RBIs, 41 stolen bases, and won his second Gold Glove during a standout all-around season.
Alvarez batted a career-high .316 with 42 home runs and 106 RBIs to become Houston's first AL MVP since 2017.
body: Pete Crow-Armstrong was unanimously named the National League’s Most Valuable Player on Thursday after the Chicago Cubs center fielder produced a spectacular all-around season.

Crow-Armstrong joined Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez as a first-time MVP winner. Alvarez was the unanimous American League winner after making a run at the Triple Crown, batting a career-high .316 with 42 home runs and 106 RBIs for the AL West champions.

Crow-Armstrong set career highs by batting .280 with 45 homers, 107 RBIs and 41 stolen bases in 162 games. He tied Kyle Schwarber for the major league lead in home runs and led the NL in runs (119), slugging percentage (.570) and OPS (.942).

He was also one of the majors’ premier defensive players. The Southern California native won his second Gold Glove and led the majors with 26 Outs Above Average and 23 Runs Prevented, according to Baseball Savant.

“You spend your whole life in baseball and you just don’t see this happen on a baseball field,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell said after Crow-Armstrong homered twice in an 8-4 win over Atlanta on 16 September. “You’re grateful to be a part of it. You’re grateful to see things like this and then you’re grateful that the fans get to see a season like this.”
Alvarez led the majors in batting average and finished tied for second in the AL in homers and second outright in RBIs, trailing Pete Alonso’s 43 homers and 113 RBIs for Baltimore.

Alvarez was Houston’s primary designated hitter, but his offensive brilliance was enough to overcome his limited defensive contributions. The four-time All-Star also led the majors in walks (109), on-base percentage (.432) and slugging percentage (.601).

The 29-year-old Alvarez became the first AL MVP from Houston since José Altuve in 2017. He received all 30 first-place votes in balloting by the Baseball Writers’ Association of America. Tampa Bay third baseman Junior Caminero, who batted .276 with 42 homers and 101 RBIs, finished second, receiving 27 of 30 second-place votes. Kansas City shortstop Bobby Witt Jr finished third.
Alvarez made his major league debut with Houston in 2019, batting .313 with 27 homers and 78 RBIs in just 87 games to earn the AL Rookie of the Year award.
He was the ALCS MVP in 2021 and helped the Astros win the 2022 World Series. He is a career .300 hitter with 212 homers and 599 RBIs in eight major league seasons.
The 24-year-old Crow-Armstrong, who agreed to a six-year, $115m contract in March, is the Cubs’ first NL MVP since Kris Bryant in 2016.
Crow-Armstrong was selected by the New York Mets in the first round of the 2020 amateur draft before being traded to Chicago in the Javier Báez deal in July 2021.
He enjoyed a breakout season in 2025, helping the Cubs qualify for the playoffs for the first time since 2020. He batted .247 with 31 homers, 95 RBIs and 35 stolen bases in 157 games.

Crow-Armstrong made significant strides at the plate in his fourth season, particularly against left-handed pitching. He batted .280 against left-handers in 2026 after hitting just .188 against them the previous year.

“I would say, like, what contributed to making myself a consistent quality at-bat and all that stuff is just, like, getting to know the strike zone just that much better,” Crow-Armstrong said before the playoffs. “I definitely missed less pitches in the zone, in the heart of the zone, that I should be hitting this year.”

articles.headline: 'Wrong' and 'nonsense' - Cummins on Khawaja sandpaper claims
keyFacts: Australia captain Pat Cummins called former team-mate Usman Khawaja's autobiography claims about the 2018 sandpaper scandal 100% wrong and complete nonsense.
Khawaja claimed in his new book that the entire Australia team, including Cummins, knew about the ball-tampering scheme and should take responsibility.
Cummins held a media conference to deny any prior knowledge of the plot, though he will not take legal action regarding the claims.
body: - Published
Australia captain Pat Cummins has hit back at former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims over the sandpaper scandal, calling them "100% wrong" and "utter nonsense".
In 2018, Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished for a plot to tamper with the ball using sandpaper in Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town.

Khawaja has published his autobiography this week and the former batter has said the entire Australia team, which included Cummins, knew about the sandpaper scheme and should have taken responsibility.

But in an extraordinary 68-minute address to the media in Sydney, Cummins countered and said: "When he says we all knew, if by that he means we knew sandpaper was going out on the field, he's 100% wrong.
"I said that consistently for the last eight years. I did not know that was happening.
"He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense."
Cummins and Khawaja played 56 Tests together until Khawaja retired from international cricket in January.
Khawaja was in the Australia XI when Cummins made his Test debut in 2011 and the pair were also once team-mates in domestic cricket with New South Wales.
"Usman is a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations," said Cummins.
"In his book he's been casual with my life and the lives of many others - and, I think, Australian cricket.
"I support him to tell his story, 100%, I'm glad he feels like he can, but we have to be accountable for the things that we say and do."
In a media conference he arranged himself, Cummins began by promising to answer all questions because, he said: "I don't want to talk about this again after today."
At times emotional, Cummins addressed a wide range of topics, including:
- Advice that some of Khawaja's claims are defamatory, but he will not take legal action
- He had been in contact with Khawaja and Smith since the book was published, but not Warner
- His belief that the one-year bans handed to Smith and Warner, and a nine-month suspension to Bancroft were "heavy handed"
- He had no recollection of Australia tampering with the ball in the 2017-18 Ashes series against England
- He had met with Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg, who has reviewed the files from the original investigation
- Explaining why sandpaper would have been present in the dressing room and that it was sometimes used by bowlers in training in order to practise with a reverse-swinging ball
Khawaja's allegations have reopened the debate about the sandpaper plot, the investigation into the cheating, the culture of Australian cricket and the reputations of those involved.
The story has dominated the media in Australia and caused headlines around the cricketing world.
Khawaja has been supported by Warner and Chadd Sayers, a seam bowler who was part of the Australia squad on the 2018 tour of South Africa.

However, his allegations have been rejected by Darren Lehmann, who was then the Australia head coach and former England batter Graeme Hick, one of Lehmann's assistants. Mitchell Starc, another bowler on the tour, has also denied Khawaja's claims.

Khawaja has put a spotlight on Cummins and his fellow bowlers Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon. The four were Australia's attack in Cape Town and remain their first-choice bowlers eight years later.
The quartet have always denied any knowledge of the plot, including in the release of a joint-statement in 2021.
In his book - Sabr - Khawaja alleged Australia were urged to find ways of getting the ball to swing by a coach, while Bancroft was later encouraged to cheat.
Khawaja also said he asked for the entire team to take responsibility for the controversy in Cape Town, but his request was rejected by two unnamed players.
Cummins said he does not recall any suggestion that the team should have shared the responsibility, or that it was rejected.

On the idea that the whole team were aligned in a plot to tamper with the ball, he said: "There was no masterplan around using illegal methods. People assume you've gone from very legal methods to suddenly taking sandpaper, and there must have been some huge masterplan.
"That is not the case. There's no grand plan. There's no team meeting. There's no bowlers saying this is what must happen."
"There's big leaps where Usman is being vague."
In his book, Khawaja detailed how he was not interviewed as part of the investigation despite sitting next to Bancroft in the changing rooms during the Test at Newlands.
Both Khawaja and Warner have criticised the investigation, which Greenberg has said he will not reopen.

Cummins confirmed he has met with Greenberg and, although the captain said he did not want to break a "confidence", that Greenberg has reviewed the sandpaper files since the release of Khawaja's book and found the accounts in the investigation to be "consistent".

Cummins has played 77 Tests for Australia and has been captain sine 2021. He said he has seen only one instance of ball-tampering in his career, during a domestic Sheffield Shield match, when a player took a bottletop on to the field.
However, he did admit that balls can sometimes be altered during training sessions, if bowlers want to practise in a certain way, or batters want to face a ball of a particular condition.
Cummins said it was not unknown for training balls to be scuffed in such circumstances, using sandpaper or even a Stanley knife.

When it was put to Cummins that he, as a bowler, must have suspected that the Cape Town ball had been tampered with, the 33-year-old described that bowlers often touch a ball as little as possible, in order to keep it dry and in a state where it will reverse-swing.

At the time of the sandpaper scandal, Cummins was 24 and playing in his 13th Test. Asked about a potential culture of ball-tampering in that era, Cummins said he noticed things then that he now realises could have been cheating.
On why Khawaja has chosen to speak now, at the end of his career, rather than in the intervening eight years, Cummins said the episode could have "weighed heavy" on the left-hander.

Addressing the culture of the Australia team eight years ago, Cummins said: "I didn't like the way we spoke to umpires, the opposition. I think there was a bit of an arrogance and a bit of an ugliness at times that didn't sit well with me as a young guy.
"Now I'm captain, I have spent a lot of time making sure that that's not the case."
Analysis - Cummins did not dodge a single question
Khawaja's claims - in his book, in interviews and on social media - have re-opened old wounds in Australian cricket, drawing battlelines that have verged on civil war.
Over the past few days, constant questions have been asked of who knew what and if the truth has been covered up in the intervening eight years.
The most pressure has been on the bowlers who played for Australia in Cape Town, - none more so than Cummins, given his rise to the captaincy.
He has been urged to front up, to show leadership. In a remarkable news conference in an indoor cricket centre in Sydney, Cummins did just that.

Others connected to the scandal who have faced the media in the past few days â Lehmann, Starc and Mitchell Marsh â have almost implicated themselves with vague responses to straight questions. Not Cummins.
The captain did not duck or dodge any of the subjects that were thrown at him by a huge throng of assembled journalists. He did so without any intervention from a media manager.
What was most striking was his criticism of Khawaja, once a team-mate and friend. In being so forceful of his rejection of what Khawaja has claimed, Cummins appeared to be a reliable witness.
The question is whether this will be enough to end the speculation. Khawaja is sure to have another say. So too Warner, who is yet to release a book of his own.
Cummins cannot prove a negative, so can use only his words when it comes to convincing the world he was not involved in the sandpaper plot.
On this occasion, Cummins was impressive. Still, when he says he never wants to talk about sandpaper again, that feels like wishful thinking.

articles.headline: MLB awards 2026: Full list of finalists, winners for MVP, Rookie of the Year, Cy Young and more
keyFacts: Major League Baseball announced the end-of-season award winners and finalists for the 2026 season across categories like MVP, Cy Young, and Rookie of the Year.
Major League Baseball awards winners included Yordan Alvarez for AL MVP, Pete Crow-Armstrong for NL MVP, Cam Schlittler for AL Cy Young, and Jacob Misiorowski for NL Cy Young.

Manager and rookie awards included Will Venable winning AL Manager of the Year, Pat Murphy winning NL Manager of the Year, Kevin McGonigle winning AL Rookie of the Year, and Sal Stewart winning NL Rookie of the Year.
body: With Major League Baseball heading into the offseason, the league had one final piece of business left from 2026: the end-of-season awards.

Throughout the week, MLB announced winners of prestigious awards like MVP, Cy Young, and Rookie of the Year, giving the season's best players the praise they deserve. In some cases, the awards felt wrapped already, but there are a few close races that came down to the bitter end.

In the past two years, Aaron Judge, Shohei Ohtani, Tarik Skubal, and Paul Skenes dominated this time of year, but for the most part, there is some new blood that rose to prominence in 2026. As a result, many of this year's winners are first-timers.
While SN's awards — which are voted on by players, managers and GMs — were previously announced, here's a look at who won MLB's awards in 2026, as voted by the BBWAA.
2026 MLB award winners
AL MVP
Winner

Yordan Alvarez, Astros: Alvarez had a career year in 2026, reaching over 40 home runs for the first time in his career while leading the league with a .316 batting average and a 1.033 OPS. Had it not been for Pete Alonso's 43 homers, Alvarez may have even won the triple crown award. The designated hitter was finally healthy for a full season, playing in 158 games and almost taking 700 plate appearances. While designated hitters are rarely in play to win the MVP, this shows just how special of a hitter that Alvarez is.
Finalists

Junior Caminero, Rays: No player in the American League has more home runs than Caminero over the last two seasons, totaling 87 long balls. This year, though, Caminero showed improved patience at the plate as he made his second consecutive All-Star game, continuing to grow as a young slugger. It helps that the Rays were the best team in the American League, with Caminero being Tampa Bay's most fearsome hitter at the plate for 162 games. Caminero could also make history as the Rays' first MVP award winner.

Bobby Witt Jr., Royals: No player was hurt more by Aaron Judge's MVP dominance in 2024 and 2025 than Witt, who had two MVP-caliber seasons in those two years. In 2026, though, Witt's offensive numbers took a slight dip, but he stole 45 bases for the first time since 2023 and continued his production as one of, if not the best, defensive shortstops in the game. Witt is a true five-tool player, with strength all around the diamond, and it feels like a matter of time before he takes home an MVP award.
NL MVP
Winner

Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs: Overtaking Shohei Ohtani as the MVP favorite required a special season, and that's exactly what PCA provided in 2026. The Cubs center fielder led all of baseball with 45 home runs and had the best OPS in the National League at .943, all while stealing 41 bases and playing elite defense in center field. Crow-Armstrong's 9.8 bWAR also led the league, putting his season in the same tier as Mike Trout, Mookie Betts, and Aaron Judge had in years past. An MVP win would make Crow-Armstrong the third all-time with a 40-40 season, joining Ohtani and Ronald Acuna Jr.
Finalists

Shohei Ohtani, Dodgers: From 2021-25, Ohtani won four MVP awards by wowing the baseball world with his pitching, hitting, and baserunning. This year, however, injuries limited Ohtani's output, as he only pitched in half a season and had his lowest home run total in a 162-game season since 2019. It's a testament to Ohtani's success as a two-way player that he is even a finalist for the MVP award once again, as no player in baseball can do as much on the field as Ohtani can.

Brice Turang, Brewers: Turang represents the World Series champion Brewers in MVP voting after he had his best season as a big-leaguer. The second baseman had career highs in home runs, RBIs, and OPS, but it's his baserunning and defense that truly separates him from the rest. Turang put up a 7.3 bWAR this season despite totaling just 21 home runs, which shows how much value he brings on the margins. Very few people expected Turang to ever compete for MVP awards, but his value for the Brewers cannot be overstated.
AL Cy Young
Winner

Cam Schlittler, Yankees: In a rotation full of aces, Cam Schlittler rose above the rest to take the mantle as the best pitcher on the Yankees. The right-hander showed what he can do last season, and he was even better in 2026 with a league-leading 1.95 ERA and 7.0 bWAR in 193.2 innings pitched. What made Schlittler's performance even more impressive is that he did all this in New York, where so many players fold under the pressure. A Cy Young win makes Schlittler the seventh Yankee to win the award and puts his name up there with some elite company.
Finalists

Dylan Cease, Blue Jays: Cease's first year with the Blue Jays after signing a lengthy contract couldn't have gone any better. The veteran put up a 2.40 ERA in 29 games, continuing to provide durability and taking the mantle as the ace of the Toronto staff. It wasn't a career-best season, as Cease was the Cy Young runner-up in 2022 with a 2.20 ERA for the White Sox, but he did reach a career high with 239 strikeouts in the season. While the Blue Jays took a step back in 2026, Cease did everything in his power to keep the team afloat through the Summer.

Parker Messick, Guardians: Messick was the best rookie pitcher in baseball this season, as his 2.56 ERA and his 6.3 bWAR vaulted him to the top of the Guardians rotation. Messick flashed last year in seven games, and he only built on that when he threw 186.1 innings in his first full season for a Cleveland team that once again won the AL West. Messick was unable to unseat his two competitors for the Cy Young, but this shouldn't be the last time that he competes for this award in his career.
NL Cy Young

Jacob Misiorowski, Brewers: "The Miz" took the world by storm in 2025 when he brought his elite fastball to the majors, but he still hadn't yet learned how to pitch. That changed in 2026 as Misiorowski led baseball's best team to a title while leading the majors with a 1.80 ERA. Misiorowski's ability to not only light up the radar gun, but do so on a consistent basis makes him rare, even in an era with so many flamethrowers in the league. With one in the books, the question is more about how many Cy Youngs he will win as he enters the prime of his career.
Finalists

Cristopher Sanchez, Phillies: Cristopher Sanchez was the runner-up in this award last season, and he didn't miss a beat with a second consecutive dominant campaign. Sanchez posted a 2.91 ERA in 207 innings while leading the league in wins, with 18, and starts, with 33. For the second consecutive season, Sanchez's 8.1 bWAR led the National League, and this time it came with a career high in strikeouts. Sanchez continues to be a coup for a Phillies team that acquired him in a minor deal and helped develop him in a major way.

Chris Sale, Braves: The 2024 Cy Young winner continued his rejuvenated career with the Braves, throwing to a 2.16 ERA in 27 starts this year. That is the third-best ERA in Sale's storied career, and second-best since he became a full-time starter in 2012. At 37 years old, Sale continues to build on what is now a Hall-of-Fame career by leading the Atlanta staff, as he rose to the occasion against the league's best teams throughout the season.
MORE: 12 players who could be traded in the offseason
AL Manager of the Year
Winner

Will Venable, White Sox: Last year, Venable took over a White Sox team that lost 121 games, but it took him just two seasons to lead Chicago back to the playoffs. That turnaround is among the best in MLB history, as Venable brought a young team together and competed all year long for the AL Central division title. Simply making the playoffs is impressive, even if it was as a Wild Card, as the White Sox do not have many playoff berths in their long history.
Finalists

Kevin Cash, Rays: No one expected the Rays to be the best team in the American League in 2026, but it wasn't a total surprise with Cash at the helm. The two-time manager of the year once again led Tampa Bay to a season with 98 wins and an AL East crown, all while representing the AL in the World Series for the second time. With a second-place finish, he missed out on a list of nine other managers to win this award three times.

Chad Tracy, Red Sox: Tracy had a tall task when he took over the Red Sox from the fired Alex Cora, but he impressed all Summer. After a slow start, Tracy' club had the best winning streak of the season at 15-straight games, and no team was better from late June through July than Boston, which helped the team make it back to the playoffs. It earned Tracy a multi-year contract to stay in Boston moving forward as one of the game's rising young coaches.
NL Manager of the Year
Winner

Pat Murphy, Brewers: Murphy first three seasons as the Brewers' manager couldn't have gone any better. Milwaukee won the NL Central in the first two, then Murphy led the team to its first World Series title in 2026. In 2024 and 2025, Murphy became one of just two managers to win this award in each of his first two seasons, and another win makes history, as no manager has done it in his first three seasons.
Finalists

Don Mattingly, Phillies: The Phillies fired Rob Thomson in April, hoping for a shakeup, and it was Mattingly who righted the ship and got the Phillies back on track. Managing Philadelphia comes with so much pressure and expectations, but that wasn't an issue for someone who played his entire career in New York. Mattingly led the Phillies to a Wild Card berth and was rewarded with a contract extension to make him the full-time manager moving forward.

Walt Weiss, Braves: The Braves moved on from Brian Snitker after an underwhelming 2025 season, but stayed in-house by promoting Weiss. A former Rockies manager, Weiss immediately hit the ground running and led Atlanta back to the top of the NL East with another division title despite dealing with injuries throughout the roster. Under Weiss, the Braves once again have World Series expectations in the future.
AL Rookie of the Year
Winner

Kevin McGonigle, Tigers: McGonigle hit the ground running for the Tigers as no player in the American League had more plate appearances in 2026. The shortstop put up an .806 OPS with 18 home runs in his first MLB season, all while leading the AL with a 7.1 bWAR. Although Detroit had a disappointing season, McGonigle's immediate breakout proved he is a cornerstone piece for a team that needed that in the wake of the Tarik Skubal trade.
Finalists

Parker Messick, Guardians: Messick is the only player nominated for two awards this year, a testament to his success as a rookie. He made two Game 1 starts for the Guardians, showing that Cleveland had the confidence in him to make big starts in the playoffs. With a 2.56 ERA and his 6.3 bWAR for the year, Messick became the latest Guardians pitcher to find himself at the top of the Cleveland rotation early in his career.

Payton Tolle, Red Sox: Tolle's first full season in the majors put him atop the Red Sox rotation, as he posted a 3.03 ERA in 26 games. What makes Tolles so special is his strikeout ability, producing 171 strikeouts in 148.2 innings pitched over the course of the year. Tolle also won the hearts of baseball fans with his approach to the game, not taking his work too seriously despite bringing a ton of passion. As Boston had the game's deepest rotation in the Summer, Tolle was the one who stood out.
MORE: 5 big things to know about MLB lockout
NL Rookie of the Year
Winner

Sal Stewart, Reds: Stewart is not the most well-rounded player in the league, but he did produce on offense for the Reds at an elite rate. Stewart set the record for most RBIs by a rookie in a single season with 112, and his 32 home runs were good enough to lead the Cincinnati offense. He also chipped in 15 stolen bases, a solid number for a player who primarily plays first base, and he made his first All-Star game in the process.
Finalists

Carson Benge, Mets: Although the Mets had a miserable year, Benge was a bright spot that became a cornerstone in the outfield for years to come. The lefty hitter hit 20 home runs with 22 stolen bases in the season, all while producing a .282 batting average in the process. He also played elite defense in right field, showing off one of the game's best outfield arms time and time again. As the Mets continue to remake their team, Benge will become a stalwart.

JJ Wetherholt, Cardinals: Like McGonigle in Detroit, Wetherholt broke out with the Cardinals thanks to an all-around game that included offense, defense and baserunning. The middle infielder hit 17 home runs with 14 RBIs while playing strong defense at second base, but very well could've played every day at shortstop if the team needed him to do so. St. Louis was all about the youth in 2026, and Wetherholt was the perfect player to lead that charge.

articles.headline: Senators probe RFK Jr.'s reason for Samoa trip after letter refuting his testimony published
keyFacts: Two Democratic senators are investigating whether Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. lied to Congress.
The investigation focuses on Kennedy's testimony regarding his 2019 trip to Samoa.
The Associated Press and The Guardian published documents in August that refuted his testimony.

articles.headline: Google Catches Up to Apple, With Digital Wallet Keys for Your Physical Home Lock
keyFacts: Google announced it will start offering digital home keys in Google Wallet built on the Aliro smart lock standard.
The new feature offers hands-free unlocking using ultrawideband technology, tap-to-unlock using NFC, and multi-device syncing.
To use the feature, users need a compatible lock, an Android phone running Android 9 or later, and a Matter-enabled Google Hub.
body: Android users looking for the most high-tech ways to manage their smart locks at home just got some great news. On Tuesday, Google announced it will start offering digital keys in Google Wallet built on Aliro, a new smart lock standard.

When I tested the predictive, futuristic Schlage Sense Pro lock — which uses ultrawideband technology and Apple Home Keys in Apple Wallet — Schlage told me that other brands were adopting Aliro to bring that same seamless usability to more devices, and now the time has come.

The best thing about the lock is that it didn’t require me to tap my phone for an NFC connection or even wave it in the vicinity. The ultrawideband, or UWB tech — think of it like an advanced version of Bluetooth older locks used — sensed a key holder was coming to the door, judged my speed and trajectory based on the signals the lock was getting, and had the door unlocked by the time I reached it, with autolock features locking it back up a minute later.
More from CNET

Home keys in Google Wallet, which have already started rolling out to Public Preview users in Google Home, offer users a lot of similar tricks with the right smart locks. That’s handy not only for saving time fumbling for your phone at the door, but also if your hands are full or you’re busy talking to someone. When I tested Schlage’s version, it could sense when I was actually approaching and when I was simply walking by the door, too, so the lock didn’t randomly open.

So far, locks compatible with UWB and the “unlock on approach” feature include not only the Schlage Sense Pro ($394.98) I tested, but also the Aqara u400 ($269.99) and the European brand Nuki Keypad 2 NFC lock ($179), with more on the way. Aliro was only officially released early in 2026, so it will take time for the standard to be broadly adopted by both locks and digital wallets, especially more advanced abilities like these. The good news is that Aliro includes encryption for security, battery-life savings and other benefits, too.
A representative from Google didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
The convenience of digital keys in Google Wallet
The “unlock on approach” feature of Aliro’s standard digital wallet keys is only one of the advantages of this upgrade, so you don’t need a UWB-compatible lock to get the benefits.

According to Google, its own home keys in Google Wallet will offer NFC to tap your phone to unlock the door (no unlocking necessary), let you use the digital key across multiple locks if necessary, and sync your key across compatible devices you use. Other people in the home can add their own home keys to the Wallet, but unlike Apple’s temporary passes, Google says guests and visitors will need to get passcodes instead of digital keys of their own.

What happens if you or someone else loses their phone? In most cases, users can rely on keypad access codes to gain entry instead of the digital wallet. But these UWB locks sometimes forgo a physical key slot entirely: Schlage says its lock doesn’t have a key slot to reduce the risk of lockpicking, but that does limit emergency unlock options.
What you need to get started
Here’s where this new lock technology gets more complicated. Finding a compatible lock is only a part of unlocking all these Wallet key features.

You’ll also need an NFC-enabled Android phone running Android 9 or later, such as the Google Pixel 10 Pro or Pixel Fold. Then you’ll need a Matter-enabled Google Hub with a Thread Border Router, which is typically a separate Google device, like a Nest Hub Max, Nest Wifi Pro system or Google TV streamer.

With all that, make sure your phone, lock, Google Wallet app and Google Home app are all updated, and you should be prompted to create home keys during your lock setup. This takes only a few seconds, and you can delete them easily, just like you could with a concert ticket or credit card.

articles.headline: Donald Trump really wants Tim Cook to run Nvidia
keyFacts: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO following reports of affairs, leaving the company temporarily led by its CFO.
President Donald Trump stated on social media and a podcast that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should run Nvidia.
Apple and Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding the CEO position.
body: Jensen Huang resigned this morning as Nvidia’s CEO following reports of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Right now, the company is being led by its CFO on an interim basis. But President Donald Trump is already throwing around one person he thinks should take over the chipmaking giant: former Apple CEO Tim Cook, who stepped down from leading the company on September 1st and moved into an executive chairman role.
Donald Trump really wants Tim Cook to run Nvidia
Nvidia is looking for a new CEO, and President Trump says the former Apple CEO would be ‘a great candidate.’

Shortly after Huang’s resignation was announced today, Trump posted his idea about Cook on Truth Social: “NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump said. “A Legend replaces a Legend!”

In a new episode of Stephen A. Smith’s Straight Shooter podcast published today, Trump made his pitch for Cook again, saying that Apple “would never be what it is today” if Steve Jobs was still “around”:
Can [Huang] be replaced?

Well, you know, the expression, Anybody can be replaced? So it’s very hard to replace him, but I had an idea this morning that I sort of just released: Tim Cook. He just sort of semi-retired from Apple. He’s done one of the greatest jobs in the history of business.

I think if Tim Cook, who built Apple… If Steve Jobs were around, Apple would never be what it is today. Tim Cook took a lot of these brilliant ideas and designs and everything else from Jobs and others, and he made it into one of the great companies of the world in a fairly short period. I think Tim Cook would be a great candidate to run Nvidia.

Apple and Nvidia didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment. Cook is well-known for his ongoing relationship with President Trump, including gifting the president a 24k gold and glass statue last year. (Trump, after Cook announced his transition plan earlier this year, posted a story about having “the head of Apple calling to ‘kiss my ass.’”)
During the podcast, Trump said he spoke to Huang yesterday and that Huang is “going through hell”:
Should [Huang] have stepped down?
Well, the big thing is, was the woman a spy, and I don’t know if that’s been determined yet, but if the woman was a spy, yes, if the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different.
But I can tell you this. Somehow, he’ll end up on his feet. I mean, I know him, I know him pretty well. I always thought of him as a fine man.

I spoke to him yesterday. He’s going through hell. What he feels most badly about is his wife and family. That’s what he is, really… that’s what he told me. I’m president, and he called me. And he said, What I’ve done to my wife and family is... That’s what he talked about.
Trump, on the podcast, called Huang a “tremendous talent.” Other tech leaders have also publicly supported Huang following his resignation.

keyFacts: California Gov. Gavin Newsom said he will decide by early January whether to run for president in 2028.
Newsom revealed his timetable at the COP31 international climate conference in Turkey while criticizing President Donald Trump.
Newsom stated he will spend the next few weeks with his family before making the final determination.
body: California Gov. Gavin Newsom said he will decide by early January whether to run for president in 2028, revealing his political timetable during a trip to the COP31 international climate conference in Turkey where he criticized President Donald Trump.

“I’ll make the determination at the beginning of the year, so we’ll spend the next few weeks with the family and make a decision early January,” Newsom told Turkey’s Anadolu news agency, calling the midterm elections a “rebuke” of Trump.
Newsom’s remarks elevate yet another international trip in which he praised California’s environmental policies and attacked Trump’s retreat from global climate pacts.

Thanks for signing up!

The outgoing governor met with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to discuss expanding California’s climate partnership with Brazil, and also finalized a new climate agreement with Portugal, according to the governor’s office.

The governor and his wife Jennifer Siebel Newsom also visited a forestry training center to exchange wildfire lessons, and he joined governors and mayors — including Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz and London Mayor Sadiq Khan — at a gathering convened by UN Secretary-General António Guterres.

Newsom and his wife are currently the focus of federal investigations, and feds reportedly requested information about the Protocol Foundation’s donors and fundraisers in subpoenas. Investigators were seeking the governor’s international travel and events, and any money used for the governor’s living and personal expenses, according to the San Francisco Standard.
But new polling suggests the recent election outcomes may not bode well for Newsom, as his chances of winning the Democratic presidential nomination plunged to just 7% in prediction markets.
Newsom said this month’s election results have placed an obligation on his party to deliver.
“I’m particularly pleased with the outcome of the election, and I think the vast majority of people around the globe are very pleased with the outcome of the election as well,” he said.
For the second consecutive year, the Trump administration did not send a delegation to the annual summit, according to Newsom’s office.

Newsom’s travels also drew a jab from Democratic political strategist Steve Maviglio, who contrasted Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra’s efforts to ingratiate himself with Democratic lawmakers in Sacramento to the outgoing governor’s focus.
“This will be a refreshing change. A Governor who spends time working with the legislature instead of junkets to Turkey,” Maviglio wrote on X.
Newsom has played coy about his presidential ambitions, openly discussing the possibility while leaving himself room to walk away.
“I don’t know if she runs, but we’ll see,” Newsom said during a fly-fishing interview in Montana. “I wouldn’t run if she ran.”

The claim elicited more than a few eyerolls among those in both Democratic and Republican political circles. But Newsom described a showdown between him and Harris as “mutual assured destruction,” pointing to their overlapping networks of friends and supporters.
Newsom also said his wife and children would have to support a campaign.
“If they’re not on board,” he said, “that’s a nonstarter.”

articles.headline: DC shooting victim was building manager known to suspected gunman, police say
keyFacts: Police said building manager James Stuart was killed inside a fitness center in Washington, D.C., after gunman Matt Lambert shot him and four others before dying by suicide.
D.C. officials said the shooting stemmed from an ongoing dispute between Lambert and the condominium homeowners association regarding maintenance issues and mold.
Court filings show Lambert had filed a lawsuit against the condominium association and property management company alleging water damage and over $100,000 in damages.
body: The individual who was shot and killed in Washington, D.C.’s Logan Circle neighborhood Thursday morning has been identified as the building manager of the Metropole condominium complex with whom the gunman was involved in a dispute.

Police said James Stuart, 46, was killed inside Vida Fitness after the gunman, Matt Lambert, 55, shot him and four others before barricading himself inside his penthouse unit, where he later died after shooting himself.
The shooting appears to have stemmed from a dispute between Lambert and the homeowners association of the condominium building where he lived, according to D.C. officials.

“We do know that there has been an ongoing dispute between the suspect in this case and the building, condo, homeowners association, management regarding maintenance issues — mold and the like — that there was a civil case that he filed against them. So, we believe that it’s related to that,” interim D.C. Chief of Police Jeff Carroll said.

Lambert, a licensed emergency medicine doctor, purchased the one-bedroom penthouse unit in 2016 for approximately $1.1 million. Lambert lived in the unit, near the intersection of 15th and P streets NW, until 2024, at which point he claimed he had to move out due to the presence of black mold, according to a former Washington Post reporter who interviewed the individual last year .

Lambert later filed a lawsuit against the Metropole condominium association in D.C. Superior Court in March 2025, alleging that work on the building’s facade caused water to leak into his penthouse apartment and resulted in more than $100,000 in damages. EJF Real Estate Services, the property management company, was also named in the lawsuit.

According to the complaint, Lambert paid to have portions of his unit deconstructed and discovered what he described as black mold inside the walls. He alleged that the defendants denied the presence of mold and attempted to cover up the hole made to investigate his initial complaint.

The condominium association rejected Lambert’s accusation, instead blaming the laundry dryers at Vida Fitness, which operates below the Metropole building, for contributing to excess moisture buildup in Lambert’s apartment. The HOA filed a third-party complaint against Vida Fitness.
Lambert said in the court filings that he spent over $300,000 in remediation expenses, including work to seal leaks in his unit.

An X account apparently connected to Lambert had repeatedly complained about the building’s mold problems and the lack of repairs to his unit. The account, which used the handle “OfMiceandMold,” posted what it described as a manifesto at 8:06 a.m. Thursday, shortly before the shooting.
“My manifesto is an engineering report,” the account wrote, alongside screenshots of an engineering document detailing alleged water damage, mold, and unfinished repairs at the building.
LOGAN CIRCLE SHOOTER IDENTIFIED: WHAT TO KNOW
Lambert’s attorney in the lawsuit, Joel Braithwaite, said he had spoken to his client days prior to the shooting, and Lambert didn’t show any signs that he would resort to violence.
“I’m at a loss for how things took any sort of turn that would have us here today,” Braithwaite said.

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone strikes hit Russian data centers across six regions — forcing companies into Kazakhstan as Putin orders emergency capacity seizure
keyFacts: Ukrainian drone strikes hit data center sites across six Russian regions in October 2026, according to reports.
Russian businesses are seeking backup computing infrastructure in Kazakhstan and Belarus as domestic cloud capacity reaches its peak.
President Vladimir Putin ordered private data center operators to reserve 10 percent of their capacity for Russian information services.
body: - Russian businesses are reportedly searching abroad for safer data center locations
- Ukrainian drone strikes have allegedly disrupted facilities linked to major Russian organizations
- Kazakhstan and Belarus are attracting Russian companies seeking backup computing infrastructure
Russian businesses are seeking computing facilities outside their borders after Ukrainian drone strikes hit data center sites across several parts of the country in October 2026.
The attacks affected installations connected to major technology and financial organizations, raising concerns about whether domestic infrastructure can withstand further disruptions.
The search is intensifying as available Russian cloud capacity hits its peak, leaving companies with fewer options for securing reliable backup arrangements.
Russian companies look abroad as infrastructure risks increase
Yevgeny Svidersky, vice president of cloud services at ITGlobal.com, told Kommersant on November 10 2026 that interest in overseas facilities had increased sharply.
Kazakhstan has emerged as a particularly attractive destination, while Belarus is also being considered for hosting artificial intelligence infrastructure and backup systems.
Two additional industry sources told Kommersant that some businesses had already started transferring workloads, although the scale of those moves remains unclear.

“Companies are reconsidering their approach to business continuity and are looking for a backup site that does not depend on the network and energy infrastructure of the primary data center,” Svidersky said.

The October 2026 attacks affected facilities associated with Yandex, VK, Sberbank, and Russia's Federal Tax Service.
The six affected regions included Vladimir, Kaluga, Leningrad, Nizhny Novgorod, Ryazan, and Saratov, all located in European Russia.
Russia's infrastructure constraints extend beyond the facilities struck, with Moscow reportedly having only about 50 megawatts of unused data center capacity.
That remaining supply could accommodate approximately two to four large commercial facilities, limiting the room available for companies seeking additional domestic hosting.
Moscow's capacity shortage adds pressure as Putin orders data center reserves
Kommersant's sources estimate that nearly 90% of cloud resources nationwide are already occupied, indicating little spare capacity for sudden demand.
Against this backdrop, President Vladimir Putin has directed privately operated data centers to set aside 10% of their capacity for Russian information services.
The decree, published through Russia's official legal portal, gives operators 10 days to make the required capacity available for possible government use.
Owners may continue using the reserved resources themselves unless a government subcommission instructs them to provide capacity for designated domestic information services.
Once such an instruction arrives, operators must make the reserved resources available within 24 hours.
The arrangement gives the state a mechanism to redirect privately controlled computing resources during emergencies without permanently transferring ownership of the facilities.
Russian officials have also considered establishing AI computing facilities in Belarus and Kazakhstan.
Alexey Borshchov, an AI project business architect at Avandok, said the overseas arrangements concern geographic backup rather than wholesale relocation.

“In practice, this is about geographic redundancy rather than moving the main infrastructure. For example, some market players are already looking for backup sites simultaneously in Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan,” Borshchov said.
“Some cloud providers are discussing with clients the possibility of reserving capacity in friendly countries.”
Companies seeking overseas backup capacity may consequently face a difficult balance between reducing domestic infrastructure exposure and complying with new state requirements.

articles.headline: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
keyFacts: Fighting broke out in September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front and the national army, marking a resumption of the two-year civil war.
Federal forces quickly took control of Mekelle after the TPLF made a strategic withdrawal, though residents and witnesses report ongoing fighting and heavy artillery.
Government officials argue the war is over and operations are ongoing, while analysts debate whether the TPLF will launch a prolonged insurgency.
body: - Published
Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment.

"People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC.
After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter.
"Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion.
Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next."

Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022.

But within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into Mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force.
Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements.

Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority.
Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat.

"The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage."

Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says.
Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost.
Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC.

He says the TPLF "intentionally allowed the ENDF to advance deeper into the heartland of Tigray", where it can be isolated and confronted on favourable terrain. "We chose not to fight on terms favourable to the enemy."

The TPLF is preparing for a major counteroffensive, he says, adding that TPLF fighters have launched attacks against Ethiopian forces in several locations following their withdrawal from the region's towns, arguing that these operations demonstrated the group's continued military capability.
It is hard to get verified information from Tigray and the BBC is unable to report from there. But phone lines and the internet, which were cut when fighting broke out, have now been restored.
Residents in different parts of Tigray tell the BBC that fighting is continuing in central, northern and north-western parts of Tigray, with the use of heavy artillery and drone strikes.
Eyewitnesses around Sheraro, a town near the Eritrean border, report heavy fighting involving artillery and ground forces in recent days.

"We could hear heavy artillery fire from the Sheraro direction. People are concerned because there is no sense of security," a businessman tells the BBC on condition of anonymity. He adds that military convoys from both sides had moved towards Sheraro, while a motorcycle operator in the southern town of Yechila says military checkpoints are still active.
Memories of the devastating 2020-2022 Tigray war remain raw for many residents.
The conflict saw widespread human rights abuses and allegations of ethnic cleansing in Western Tigray, while estimates suggest the war claimed hundreds of thousands of lives.

As soldiers from Eritrea, accused of some of the worst atrocities in the previous conflict, and Ethiopia have reappeared in Tigray's towns, many residents describe a profound sense of fear and anxiety, saying the sight of the troops has reopened still-fresh wounds.

Military sources aligned with the federal army say operations against the TPLF are continuing, with recent fighting and troop movements reported in northern Tigray, near the Eritrean border, as well as across central Tigray's rugged highlands. They claim the TPLF's capabilities are being steadily degraded.

Security analysts and observers agree that unrest is likely to continue for some time. "I see a situation in which there could be a prolonged war in Tigray," Yared Tibebu, a well-known Ethiopian commentator based in the US, tells the BBC.

Yared argues that the TPLF has a long history of waging protracted armed struggles and believes the movement is once again preparing for a lengthy conflict. He believes that once the group has reorganised its military and political structures, it may attempt to resume offensive operations.
However he believes this will not happen for some time because of internal divisions - a suggestion dismissed by TPLF spokesperson Mikael.

Hudson rejects the idea that Tigray is heading towards a prolonged war but agrees that the region may not be truly peaceful for some time. "The TPLF may continue a low-level insurgency and guerrilla campaign, but that is not war. I do not think there will be a wider-scale conflict between the federal forces and the TPLF."

He says the TPLF no longer possesses the size, strength or military capability required to effectively confront federal forces, which he says have significantly expanded and modernised in recent years. "The TPLF has also lost much of its public support and cannot easily rebuild its ranks through recruitment," he says.

Yared, on the other hand, points to the TPLF's history of overcoming setbacks as evidence that the movement could recover to sustain a prolonged struggle. "The TPLF has overcome many major challenges in the past. It is wrong to conclude that it has no public support. It is a political movement with a history stretching back more than 50 years," he says.

What Yared sees as a strength, Hudson sees as a weakness, saying the TPLF is still "trapped in the past", and continues to behave as a dominant party within Tigray, even though the situation has changed. "It is a movement that has not evolved, modernised or expanded."

While Hudson argues that the TPLF is not equipped to sustain a major military campaign, the TPLF spokesman says the group obtains weapons and logistical supplies from the Ethiopian military. "We seize weapons from our enemy, and the weaponry that has entered Tigray will, sooner or later, become ours."

In early October, eyewitnesses told the BBC they had seen Eritrean troops in Tigray amid reports they were backing the TPLF. However, they appear to have returned home and Hudson thinks the country would be wary of becoming further embroiled in the conflict.

"First, Eritrea does not have unlimited resources. Second, the TPLF is no more an effective military force, and Eritrean leaders may have concluded that supporting it at this stage would not yield significant military gains," he says. "Third, Eritrea would have to consider the risk of provoking a confrontation with Ethiopia if it openly backs the TPLF."

Sources in the Ethiopia army tell the BBC that senior members of the TPLF's political leadership were briefly based in Eritrea, however, they say the authorities ordered them to leave in early November, shortly after President Isaias Afwerki returned from Russia. According to the sources, the move was driven by concerns that Ethiopia could use their presence as a reason to invade.

Hudson also argues that Eritrea's renewed diplomatic engagement with the US, whose relations with the TPLF have long been strained, could further discourage Asmara from providing meaningful support to the movement.
In September, seven Ethiopian rebel groups led by the TPLF announced the formation of a new coalition called the Alliance for Survival, aimed at removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government.

Yared believes the alliance could give the TPLF the strength to keep on fighting. "Its members can combine their strengths. The TDF [the TPLF's military wing] has leadership experience and organisational capacity, while Fano [an ethnic Amhara militia] is believed to have between 70,000 and 80,000 fighters.
"If conditions emerge that allow the forces to co-ordinate effectively, the TPLF's current difficulties may not last long," he says.

Hudson, however, rejects that argument, insisting that the alliance is unlikely to alter the balance of power. "I don't think the TPLF can be saved by this alliance. The ethnic militias have not demonstrated the capacity, either individually or collectively, to pose a serious threat to federal forces. We should not underestimate the strength of the federal army," he says.

Abraha from Mekelle University argues that the conflict in Tigray will only truly be over if the federal government addresses the region's feeling that it has been marginalised, both economically and politically by the current government.

However, many Tigrayan elites and political observers remain wary of the federal government's intentions. They question whether the authorities in Addis Ababa are genuinely seeking to address Tigray's problems, or whether they are taking advantage of the region's weakness to boost their influence.
In the meantime, many ordinary people in Tigray say their priority is peace.
"Peace seems slow in coming. Most people are tired of politics. Whatever happens, we only want peace and a chance to rebuild our lives," says Firut from her beauty salon in Mekelle.

articles.headline: The rise of 'housefishing' - when does using AI go from enhancing to misleading?
keyFacts: Estate agents are increasingly using AI to enhance property listing photos, raising concerns that the technology can mislead prospective buyers.
Property seeker Olivia Nicole said she wasted time viewing a London house where AI made rooms and structural features look different.
Trading Standards said estate agents can use AI for basic photo enhancements if labeled, but structurally changing rooms could break the law.
body: - Published
Have you ever been impressed by the pictures of a property on an estate agent's website, only to find the place looks completely different when you view it in person?
Then there's a chance that AI was used to enhance the images you saw.
From repainted walls to imaginary lawns, estate agents are increasingly using the technology to make homes seem more appealing, arguing it helps buyers visualise the potential of a place.
But experts warn it can go too far and mislead prospective buyers - a trend dubbed "housefishing".
So how much AI enhancement is too much?
'The rooms were much smaller'
Earlier this year Olivia Nicole, 29, was searching online for five-bedroom properties in south-west London when a house on Rightmove caught her eye.
But when she arrived to view it several days later she initially thought she had come to the wrong place.
"The rooms were much smaller than they were in the pictures and the decor was totally different," she tells the BBC. "Some structural features were also different."

For example, there was a raised section of the wall behind the sofa that didn't appear in the images. The windows were also noticeably smaller. Olivia was so surprised she took her own pictures of the property for comparison.
It later turned out the pictures she had seen on Rightmove, which also appeared on the Zoopla and Winkworth websites, were enhanced with AI.
But that wasn't clear in the listing, Olivia says, and she feels the agent wasted her time.
"It was frustrating, because I had taken several hours off work for the viewing which I had to make up for."
All three companies told the BBC they had strict guidelines on how AI could be used on their websites and have since taken the images down.
'A surge of AI listings'
Estate agents have long used wide-angle lens cameras or Photoshop to make homes seem bigger or more appealing to buyers, but AI is making this process much easier and more accessible.

It is difficult to quantify how common the practice is, says the Guild of Property Professionals, a trade group of independent estate agents, but it has issued guidance on how to use AI enhancement responsibly.

According to a recent survey, external of 906 UK homebuyers, one in five who had who purchased a home in the past year said they had viewed a property where the listing photos had been digitally enhanced to make the home appear better than it actually was.
Jack Bushrod reviews quirky property listings he finds on Rightmove for his social media channel, Housing Horrors, and says he has seen a "surge" of AI-enhanced images over the last six months.
He thinks using AI is fine up to a point - to declutter a busy room, or add furniture to an empty one so a prospective buyer can see its potential.
But he draws the line at anything that misleads a prospective buyer or wastes their time.
"I've seen one house where they had removed a pillar and added a window. Others might use AI to remove stains on the carpet or cracks in tiles. It's little details you would only notice in person."
He says most of the enhanced images he's seen weren't clearly labelled as AI-generated.
Cara, 38, is currently selling her home in Lowestoft, Suffolk, and says she was surprised when she saw the AI-enhanced pictures of her property her estate agent, Howards, put on Rightmove.
In one photo, her son's room was completely emptied of toys and clutter.
In another, of her daughter's room, the agent appears to have removed a doll's house, brightened the room, and used AI to change the shape of a rug, but that image has since been taken down.
Cara has had several viewings so far and says that one person has commented on the differences. But she says she trusts Howards, which has acknowledged the use of AI in the property listing.
"If they'd changed something structurally or it was really wild and didn't look like our home at all then I would put my foot down," she says.

A spokeswoman told the BBC that Howards had now introduced a policy of labelling all AI-enhanced photos. She added that the firm never used AI "to misrepresent the fundamental features of a property".
"It's about helping people imagine the possibilities, not changing the reality of what's being sold."
'Jumping on the bandwagon'

Trading Standards told the BBC that estate agents can use AI to make basic enhancements to photos, or to virtually furnish an empty room or garden, as long as they indicate they have used the technology.
But it says structurally changing a room, for example by adding a window, or hiding features could mislead consumers and break the law.
Jack Bushrod thinks all estate agents should have to clearly label AI-enhanced photos and mention any use of the tech prominently in the key features slide of a property listing.
He also expects to see more housefishing as time goes on.
"My worry is the more estate agents use AI, others will see the trend and jump on the bandwagon."
Additional reporting by Star McFarlane

articles.headline: All Treasure Rooms in Queen’s Domain and how to find them
keyFacts: Queen’s Domain contains five secret Treasure Rooms that offer valuable rewards and require specific items like Keystones to open.
Players must first obtain Keystones, starting with the first one found near Obmuer Temple after locating Aganmi’s missing raider.
The five hidden areas consist of two Blood Treasure Rooms, two Velvet Treasure Rooms, and one Jade Treasure Room.
body: Queen’s Domain has five Treasure Rooms, and locating them can be a difficult task. These secret areas are challenging to find, but they offer valuable rewards. In this guide, I will make things easy for you to find all five of them.
Table of contents
How to find all Treasure Rooms in Queen’s Domain Blood Treasure Rooms

How to find all Treasure Rooms in Queen’s Domain
Before we can venture to find the treasure vaults, the first task is to get the Keystones. You will need them to open the vaults. Once you reach Obmuer Temple, you can find the first Keystone.

Screenshot by Destructoid Make your way through the water until you’ll reach a point where a broken structure will slope upwards. Go past it and use the edge to air dash to move forward. You’ll come across a small plot of land where you find one of Aganmi’s missing raiders.

From there, you’ll find an opening in the temple to your right. Drop, and then turn left to find the dark cave. Continue straight, and you’ll find a ledge that drops into a large room with pillars. Go to the other side of the room, enter the open vault, and you’ll find a skeleton sitting with a note next to it.
Read this note to get the Blood Keystone from the shop for 24 Ancient Coins.
Blood Treasure Rooms

There are two Blood Treasure Rooms, and you can find the first one in the basement of the Tower of Knowledge. Once you defeat the boss, clear the growths. This allows you to access a room filled with candle crawlers.
Screenshot by Destructoid Clear out the enemies, and you’ll discover the door to the Blood Vault. Inside, you’ll get the Rusted Greatsword.
To find the next Blood Vault, head to Verdant Hollow. Go through the Petrified Garden and walk out of the gate that connects the Rotting Cavern and Verdant Hollow.
arkasarkar2304@ You can do so using the elevator from the Verdant Hollow wing alter. Walk into the cave from the ledge, and you’ll find the dark room.
Velvet Treasure Rooms

Screenshot by Destructoid Head to Neasied to find the first Velvet Treasure Room. You will find a cave on one side of the area that has the altar on the cliff face. Enter the cave and go all the way down to find a hole. This hole will lead you to another room. Follow the path, and you will eventually reach the elevator that takes you all the way down. You will find the treasure room entrance at this location.

Screenshot by Destructoid To find the next one, head to the Rotting Cavern. Look for a shine-like structure and follow the path that leads you to it. Eventually, you will come across a sealed door that requires four dark triangular slit pieces. You can find these pieces around the area, and I believe their locations are random. Once you find them, it will lead you to the vault.
Jade Treasure Room

There is only one jet treasure room, and you will find it in the Deimpo Mausoleum. Go to the wing altar and take the door on the right. This will lead you to a giant stairwell, and as you descend, you will find the door to the vault.
