articles.headline: Wolfenstein 3 Confirmed to Be in Development at MachineGames
keyFacts: Developer MachineGames and id Software confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is officially in development.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and the developers announced the production on social media during Xbox Fanfest.
Actors Brian Bloom and Debra Wilson will return to their roles using motion capture.
body: As part of the Xbox's 25th anniversary celebration at Xbox Fanfest in Seattle today, developer MachineGames and franchise creators id Software confirmed what had long been rumored : that Wolfenstein 3 is in development.

MachineGames will once again be developing it. Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossus was released to rave reviews in 2017, but MachineGames then put the series on hold to develop 2024's absolutely stellar Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.

But now, Wolfenstein is back on the front burner at the Swedish studio. "Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at Machine Games," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed on X. "One of gaming’s most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more."

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvh
— ASHA (@asha_shar) November 12, 2026

id Software and MachineGames added on to Sharma's post, which shows a page of the Wolfenstein 3 script, saying simply , "His reputation precedes him," referring to the action described on the script page. "Wolfenstein 3 is in production." The developers also confirmed that actors Brian Bloom (as B.J. Blazkowicz) and Debra Wilson (as Grace Walker) will return via a photo of the pair in the developer's motion-capture studio.

Wolfenstein 3 shouldn't come as much of a surprise. Last year, in an interview with Noclip , MachineGames studio head Jerk Gustafsson said the team had "always seen [BJ's story] as a trilogy," adding: "That journey for BJ, even during those first weeks at [id Software], when we mapped out New Order — we still had the plan for at least [BJ], what would happen in the second one and what would happen in the third one.
"I think that's important to say, because⁠ — at least, I hope ⁠— we're not done with Wolfenstein yet. We have a story to tell."

That's not all that Wolfenstein fans have to look forward to, as the pioneering first-person shooter series is also being developed into a TV series at Amazon. Xbox's official 25th anniversary is this Sunday, November 15, while id Software celebrates its 35th anniversary this year.

articles.headline: DOJ takes aim at $1.2B in Binance loot as FBI disrupts North Korean scam
keyFacts: The US government said it obtained court authorization to seize over $1.2 billion stolen during last month's Binance heist.
The FBI said it disrupted a North Korean social engineering scheme called FaceStealer that amassed over $400 million.
Investigators said the scheme used fake video meetings and malware to target cryptocurrency workers and steal webcam videos.
body: The US government on Thursday said it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain use of over $1.2 billion stolen during last month's $6.3 billion Binance heist, as part of a larger effort to disrupt North Korea's ongoing cryptocurrency theft.

The court also allowed the takedown of cloud-based infrastructure used in a Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) social engineering scheme called “FaceStealer” that has amassed more than $400 million in the last 18 months.

It’s called FaceStealer because it involved secretly recorded webcam videos. Victims are typically people working in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, along with open source software developers and maintainers who DPRK hackers target in the hope of accessing the software repositories they control as the first step towards creating supply chain attacks.
900+ faces stolen
The FBI said it had seized more than 900 webcam videos belonging to these tech workers.
Here’s how the attack works.
First, the North Koreans send targets an invitation to join a video meeting. Those invitations come from hijacked accounts that the next intended victim may find familiar or credible.

“You're going to think it's real because it's going to be based on either conversations or interests you've expressed in the past with this actual person,” said special agent Jeremy Robertson, who oversees counterintelligence and cyber investigations at FBI Los Angeles.
“They're going to then send you a link to catch up, and it's usually a calendar invite, and it's going to have some typo-squatted URLs in there,” he told reporters on Thursday.

The URL directs the victim to a fake Zoom or Teams meeting, and the cybercriminals record the target’s webcam video while playing a phony, prerecorded video of the person who purportedly sent the meeting invite.
Sometimes the hackers also use deepfake videos of well-known individuals in the cryptocurrency and web3 industries, we’re told.

“When you log in, whoever invited you – your friend or business associate – is going to be on the screen, but you're not going to hear any audio,” Robertson said. “But you're going to see their face, you're going to see them looking around, you're going to see them mouthing some words, and then in the text box you're going to receive some instructions.”
‘You’re on mute’ as a social engineering vector

The text box tells the victim that the person on the other end of the video call can’t hear them, they need to upgrade their software for the audio to work properly, and it sends a link to the supposed fix.
Clicking to access the “fix” installs cryptocurrency-stealing malware on the victim’s computer and sends their contact list to the digital thieves to perpetuate the scam.

The FBI attributes FaceStealer to a North Korea-linked group tracked as Sapphire Sleet , which is widely regarded as a Lazarus Group offshoot. Sapphire Sleet is also known as UNC1069, Stardust Chollima, APT38, and BlueNoroff.

“The actors behind this activity, commonly referred to as Sapphire Sleet and other associated names, are part of a broader North Korean effort to generate revenue for the regime, to steal virtual assets, and gain access to networks and trusted online ecosystems,” Brett Leatherman, assistant director of the FBI's Cyber Division, told reporters. “North Korean hackers are increasingly blending cyber intrusion, social engineering, and emerging technologies such as deep fakes to make their impersonation efforts more convincing and scalable.”
Binance heist update

The FBI also provided an update on its efforts to recover the stolen assets from the October 29 attack on Binance. The agency previously blamed the $6.3 billion heist on TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking operation also linked to Lazarus Group.

Last week, Binance revealed the attackers laid the groundwork for their “ sophisticated, multi-stage campaign ” back in June, and said it involved social engineering during fake job interviews, malware downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint takeover, and an “advanced transaction-authorization method.”

Since the theft, federal investigators and private-sector partners have helped freeze more than $2.7 billion in stolen assets. The Justice Department's court authorization covers more than $1.2 billion of that haul.®

articles.headline: Lefty freshmen lawmakers known as ‘The Bloc’ swarm Capitol Hill for cringey photos
keyFacts: Newly elected left-wing lawmakers known as The Bloc gathered on the Capitol steps Thursday for group photos during congressional orientation.
The informal coalition of progressive representatives has been coordinating strategy and supporting each other politically since their primary campaigns.
More than 100 incoming congressmen are attending a 10-day crash course in Washington on how to serve in federal office.
body: The group of newly elected left-wing insurgent lawmakers, dubbed “The Bloc,” gathered on the steps of the Capitol Building Thursday to pose for cringey, yearbook-style photos.

Reps.-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier (D-NY), Claire Valdez (D-NY), Brad Lander (D-NY), Melat Kiros (D-Colo.), Adam Hamawy (D-NJ), Donavan McKinney (D-Mich.), Daniel Biss (D-Ill.), Dan Koh (D-Mass.), Chris Rabb (D-Pa.), Angela Gonzales-Torres (D-Calif.), Frederick Haynes III (D-Texas) and Patty Garcia (D-Ill.) were among the crew of progressives that huddled together during a break from the orientation programming.
Political journalists and insiders have been using the moniker “The Bloc” to refer to the informal coalition of lefty lawmakers since at least September.
The name appears to refer to how the group has been coordinating strategy and supporting one another politically since the primaries.
“They’re moving as a bloc,” a progressive operative told Politico in September.

The gang — which is apparently differentiating itself from the “Squad” group of lefty pols led by Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.) — represents just a fraction of the more than 70 new Democrats elected in the midterm blue wave.

Rep. Analilia Mejía (D-NJ), wearing a bright blue dress, stood front and center of the incoming “Bloc” members. Mejía, a former top campaign aide to democratic socialist Sen. Bernie Sanders, was elected to replace Mikie Sherrill in New Jersey’s 11th Congressional District last year.
When the photo shoot wrapped, several of the lefty pols shared selfies on social media that gave off strong first-day-of-school vibes.
“A freshman class that looks like America,” Koh, seen flashing deuces, posted on Facebook.
In an Instagram post, McKinney appropriately accompanied his photos from “Freshman Class Picture Day” rapper Gucci Mane’s song “Photo Shoot.”

“It’s going to take all of us, from New Jersey and New York to Bakersfield and Los Angeles to help build a brighter future,” Gonzales-Torres, a DSA-backed Democrat from Los Angeles, wrote in her Instagram post.
“When people unite behind a purpose, there are no limits,” she added, including music from South Central LA legend Ice Cube.
More than 100 incoming congressmen descended on Washington this week for a 10-day crash course on the procedures for how to serve in federal office.

articles.headline: Cummins dismisses Khawaja's sandpaper claims as 'utter nonsense'
keyFacts: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismissed Usman Khawaja's autobiography claims that the team knew about the 2018 ball-tampering as utter nonsense.
Khawaja wrote in his book 'Sabr' that the entire Australian team was aware of the Cape Town sandpaper scheme.
Cummins stated he will not pursue legal action over the defamation, adding that the team must move on after eight years.
body: Sandpapergate: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismisses Usman Khawaja's claims over ball-tampering scandal as 'utter nonsense'

Usman Khawaja said in new book 'Sabr' that every Australia player was aware of ball-tampering scheme in Cape Town in 2018; current Test captain Pat Cummins, who played in the match, reiterated his denial of involvement and dismissed Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense"
Friday 13 November 2026 00:11, UK

Australia Test captain Pat Cummins dismissed his former team-mate Usman Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense" after the recently retired batter said in his autobiography that the whole side were aware of ball-tampering that took place on their 2018 tour of South Africa.

Khawaja made the revelations in his new book 'Sabr', which was released earlier this week, bringing the scandal back onto the agenda eight years after Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera using sandpaper on the ball while Australia were fielding.

Only Bancroft, then-captain Steve Smith and his vice-captain David Warner were punished, with each receiving lengthy bans as the rest of the Australian team and coaching staff denied knowledge of the scheme.

Cummins, who was a relatively junior member of the side playing in just his 13th Test match, in 2021 issued a joint-statement with fellow bowlers from the fixture Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, in which they denied knowing that a foreign substance had been taken onto the field to alter the ball in order to try to make it swing.

"When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he's 100 per cent wrong. I've said that consistently for the last eight years," Cummins told reporters on Friday morning in Sydney having called the press conference himself on social media.
"I did not know that was happening, but Usman actually says things that are actually far more serious than that.
"He says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense."

Following the publication of the book, Warner, who received a year-long ban from all cricket and a lifetime ban from leadership roles, said on Monday that Khawaja's version of events was "100 per cent accurate".
Cummins, who was appointed Australia captain in November 2021, criticised Khawaja for being "casual" with the lives of his former team-mates and Australian cricket as a whole.
"Usman's a friend, but friends aren't casual with each other's lives and reputations," Cummins said.
"In his book, Ussie has been casual with my life and the lives of many others, and I think Australian cricket."

Cummins, who appeared to become emotional at times in a press conference that lasted more than an hour, revealed that a video taken of him and his wife Becky in a heated discussion a day earlier had been prompted by her anger with Khawaja's actions.
Despite that and his clear disagreement with Khawaja's statements, Cummins said that he does not intend to pursue legal action.
"I did get advised this week that some of the things that've been said are probably defamatory, but I won't be doing that," Cummins said.
"You've got to move on. It's been eight years. We're moving on. So you got to draw a line at some point."

Cummins has been rested for England's white-ball tour of Australia, which resulted in him holding his press conference on Friday morning in Sydney just hours before the first ODI was scheduled to begin in Perth.
How have other Australian players reacted?

Cummins' extraordinary press conference came a day after Australia ODI captain Mitchell Marsh, who was also part of the team that toured South Africa in 2018, declined to comment on a series of questions about Khawaja's book.
Khawaja also claimed in the book that Australia experimented with lifting the seam on the ball during the 2017-18 Ashes at home to England, which they won 4-0 under the captaincy of Smith.
Starc, who had spoken to reporters on Tuesday, took a similar line to Cummins as he insisted that his recollections hadn't changed.
Starc, who is also not part of Australia's limited-overs side to face England, said of Khawaja's claims: "I haven't really paid much attention to it to be fair.
"There are differing opinions of eight years ago. We were heavily grilled through the process, at the time and since.
"I won't speak on behalf of the bowlers but from where I stand my opinion hasn't changed, my recollection hasn't changed from what we said in 2021.
"As far as our statement said, we weren't aware of things being taken on the field. That's where I'll leave it.
"I will be sticking to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time eight years ago, so clearly there are differing versions from different people.
"We weren't aware of anything taken on the field to be tampered with. We saw it on the big screen in Cape Town.
"As far as the book is concerned, I haven't read it. I probably won't read it, so that's for Usman to elaborate on."

articles.headline: Meta's Muse can now make calls on your behalf (if you have a paid subscription)
keyFacts: Meta's AI agent Muse can now place phone calls to businesses on behalf of users who have a paid subscription, according to Meta.
Meta's Chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said the new feature can handle tasks like scheduling appointments and making reservations.
Users like Meta employee Matt Schlicht reported that the AI successfully managed tasks such as waiting on hold for information.
body: Meta's Muse can now make calls on your behalf (if you have a paid subscription)
The AI agent can schedule appointments, make reservations and wait on hold for you.

Meta's Muse just got another ability that could make the AI agent feel a little bit more like an actual personal assistant. Muse is now able to place phone calls on your behalf, if you have a paid subscription.

With the change, Muse is able to call businesses to help with tasks like making reservations, scheduling appointments and other "calls you don't want to make," Meta's Chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said in an update. The feature is available to those who have paid for a separate Muse subscription, which comes with additional tokens and some extra features.

Some users who have had access to the feature already have reported that Muse has been able to handle phone-related tasks with relative ease. Moltbook creator and Meta Superintelligence employee Matt Schlicht shared a recreation of a phone conversation his agent had with a Volvo dealership last month, noting that it was able to wait on hold in order to get the info he needed.
My muse called Volvo for me to see when the next available appointment is.
You can listen to the phone call here.
I have it do multiple calls like this every day (I'm still trying to get better and better at leveraging muse).
My muse called, waited on the line for 15 minutes,... pic.twitter.com/bosH1tyW1R
— Matt Schlicht (@MattPRD) October 9, 2026

Interestingly, in the call shared by Schlicht, Muse doesn't explicitly identify itself as an AI agent though it notes it's calling his behalf and that it's transcribing the call. That may be enough for some straightforward tasks, but there's always a chance these types of calls could go off the rails or the person on the other end hangs up when they realize they're speaking with an AI.

Meta has been steadily churning out new features for Muse, which has already drawn more than 10 million users, according to the company. People can also now assign a dedicated email address to their agent in order to loop it into important emails without giving wholesale access to their inbox.

The company isn't the first to experiment with phone-calling abilities for AI. Google has introduced a number of similar features over the years, including "Call For Me" for Pixel phones and Instinct recently introduced a "Concierge" feature for its agent that's meant to handle more complex calls.

articles.headline: Desire Doue forced off with gruesome tooth injury
keyFacts: France player Desire Doue suffered a dislodged tooth after being hit in the face by Italy player Davide Frattesi.
Italy defeated France in the Nations League match, handing manager Zinedine Zidane his first defeat.
France manager Zinedine Zidane stated he hopes Kylian Mbappe will be available to face Turkey on Sunday.
body: Desire Doue’s tooth got dislodged after a nasty tangle during France’s Nations League defeat against Italy.
The French international received an elbow in the face by Davide Frattesi that dislodged his tooth.
It was a very unfortunate incident, but it left Doue in a world of pain Getty
It was a total accident, but the blow did serious damage to his teeth, and the forward was immediately taken off.
It happened towards the end of the game, with Senny Maylu of Paris Saint-Germain replaced him.
The PSG star indicated that he required medical attention that he received on the field before Zinedine Zidane took him off.
View Tweet: https://t.co/di3jTmWZhT
Story of the game
Italy dealt out a first defeat to Zidane as France manager as the Azzurri moved top of their Nations League .
It takes who wins the group to the final game with just a point separating Belgium, France and Italy.
Things started very well for Les Bleus as well as Michael Olise opened the scoring on ten minutes after a costly error by Gianluigi Donnarumma.
But the scores were levelled 16 minutes later as Francesco Pio Esposito continued his great form for Inter Milan with the equaliser.
And in the second half, the 2006 world champions ran away with the match.
Esposito scored from the penalty spot before Frattesi bagged three minutes later to put the game beyond France.
And after the game, Zidane said: “When we were struggling, we didn’t manage to react within the framework of the game plan that we put in place.
It’s another painful night for Zidane against Italy AFP
“We did it at 0-0 or at 1-0, but as soon as they took the lead, we were in disarray, notably defensively. We won’t be worried. It is a part of football.
“It is better that these kinds of moments come now. It wasn’t a ‘non-match’ tonight, but there is something to improve upon.”
There was no Kylian Mbappe for Les Bleus, but he could be back to face Turkey on Sunday.
They have been the whipping boys of the group losing every match so far.
France know if they win that, they stand a very good chance of topping the group.
On Mbappe’s fitness, Zidane said: “Yes, yes, I hope so! [he will be available to face Turkey].
“That’s why he stayed with us in the camp… I don’t think it’s anything serious.
“The idea is to get him back on the pitch.”

articles.headline: Democrat Cindy Holscher wins Kansas governor's race, extending party's hold on governor's mansion
keyFacts: Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher won the Kansas governor's race, defeating Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson according to AP projections.
The victory keeps the governor's mansion in Democratic hands, marking the third consecutive Kansas gubernatorial election won by a Democrat.
Masterson conceded the race, congratulated Holscher, and stated he will return to the Senate in January to focus on legislative priorities.
body: Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher won the Kansas governor’s race, defeating Republican Kansas Senate President Ty Masterson in the open contest to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly, The Associated Press projected.

The victory keeps the governor’s mansion in Democratic hands and marks the third consecutive Kansas gubernatorial election won by a Democrat. Kelly won the office in 2018 and secured a second term in 2022.

The result underscores Democrats’ continued success in Kansas gubernatorial races despite Republicans’ longstanding dominance in the state’s presidential elections. The GOP has carried Kansas in every presidential election since 1968.
GOP WIPEOUT GOES FROM BAD TO WORSE AS DEMS QUIETLY SCORE ANOTHER MAJOR WIN WITH BIG RAMIFICATIONS

Holscher has served in the Kansas Senate since 2021 after previously spending four years in the state House. She secured the Democratic nomination after defeating fellow state Sen. Ethan Corson, who was endorsed by Kelly and former Democratic Gov. Kathleen Sebelius, in the August primary.

Holscher faced scrutiny during the campaign over resurfaced social media posts from 2023 in which she suggested Jesus Christ could have been transgender. The comments came during a debate over proposed Kansas legislation restricting drag performances in front of children.
Holscher celebrated her victory in a post on X, thanking Kansas voters as she prepared to take office.
THE TOP TRUMP OFFICIALS DEMOCRATS ADMIT ARE ON THEIR HIT LIST FOR INVESTIGATIONS IN THE NEW CONGRESS
"Thank you, Kansas! It’s the honor of a lifetime to serve as your next Governor," Holscher wrote.
Masterson, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump in the crowded GOP primary, conceded the race in a post on X and said he had called Holscher to congratulate her.
"It looks like we will come up just short, but the things we fought for are no less important today than they were yesterday."

Masterson, who has served as Kansas Senate president since 2021, also pointed to Republicans' continued control of the state Legislature and said he would return to the Senate in January to focus on property taxes, public safety, affordability and schools.

articles.headline: Slay The Spire 2′s Latest Update Adds A New Character, Two New Modes, And A Byrdpip Evolution!
keyFacts: Slay the Spire 2 released beta patch v0.113.0, adding a new playable character named the Fool.
The update introduces two new game modes called Blitz Mode and Dread Mode.
The patch also includes new relics, card adjustments, events, and a Byrdpip evolution.
body: After months without any sort of new content, we finally have a new Slay the Spire 2 updateâand, well, I see what took âem so goddamn long, because Iâm not even sure where to start with this one.

Perhaps itâs best to start with the star of the show: the Fool, Slay the Spire 2âs sixth playable character. Sheâs certainly unique, even by Slay the Spire standards. Her main gimmick revolves around her Arrow which, when fired using specific cards, will inflict the Impaled status on the enemy.

When an enemy is Impaled, you have to hit them three times (or kill them) to get your Arrow back, and cards that require an Arrow wonât work until you do. Iâve only played about three games with the character so far, but they seem absurdly busted. However, thatâs why this is a beta patch, and the important thing is that the Fool is super funâsort of reminiscent of the Hermit from Slay the Spire: Downfall, actually.

And hey, spoiler alertâthe Hermit is now in Slay the Spire 2! Sort of. One of the Foolâs other unique gimmicks is that they can generate Tarot Cards of other Slay the Spire characters, including both the Hermit and the Watcher. Does this mean both of these characters are coming to Slay the Spire 2? Well, Mega Crit describes the Fool as the âfirst new character for Early Accessâ in the patch notes, so maybe?

Of course, the Fool isnât the only new addition in beta patch v0.113.0, as we also received two brand-new modes: Blitz Mode and Dread Mode. Blitz Mode is essentially a super-quick mode, but with some odd changes. Thereâs no gold, thereâs no map, and the Merchantâs shop now contains free buffs and card rewards instead of relics and specific cards. Iâve only played through this mode once, but Iâm already a big fan.

Dread Mode is, as the name may imply, an even harder version of Ascension 10. Bosses are stronger, enemies have new buffs, and you just earn random curses as you climb. Iâve not tried this mode yet, although I am, quite aptly, dreading it. I already get my ass handed to me on Ascension 10, so god knows how rough this is gonna be.

Thereâs also a bunch of new relics, card nerfs/buffs, and even some freshly added events! There are far too many to go over here, but thereâs one specific event Iâve yet to encounter that I am very, very excited to run into: the âByrdpip evolution.â I have no idea what this will do to our little hatchable Brydpip pal, although I am hoping it makes his mohawk even cooler.

articles.headline: In reversal, American Cancer Society urges prostate cancer tests for all men
keyFacts: The American Cancer Society now recommends routine prostate cancer screening with PSA tests for all men.
Average-risk men should be tested every two years from age 50 to 69, while high-risk men should start testing at age 45.
This guidance departs from the 2010 iteration, which made no universal recommendations for routine screening.
body: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that all men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test.
Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday.

Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years.
Men ages 70 to 74 should consult their doctor on continuing screening, while those 75 and up are not recommended to get screened.

The new guidance departs from ACS’s previous iteration, published in 2010, which made no universal recommendations for routine screening. Men at age 50 were recommended to use shared-decision making with their doctors on whether or not to get tested. The recommendation was similar to that from the US Preventive Services Task Force, a federal panel that regularly evaluates evidence and makes recommendations on such preventive medical care. (The USPSTF is currently working on an update to its prostate cancer screening recommendation, though it should be noted that the panel has recently been overhauled by anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and new members are reportedly rife with conflicts of interest.)

articles.headline: Jensen Huang is out. What now?
keyFacts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an executive alleged to be a Chinese spy.
Huang played a central role in the AI industry and actively lobbied against US restrictions on chip exports to China.
Congress has called Huang to speak later this month as lawmakers seek to further restrict chip exports to China.
body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in October 2026. | Joel Saget/AFP via Getty Images

The first big sex scandal of the AI era has taken down Jensen Huang , Nvidia’s co-founder and longtime CEO. Nvidia’s board of directors announced his resignation on Thursday morning and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.

Huang has been making headlines all week after news broke Friday that he had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singaporean tech firm Megaspeed who the US government alleges was also a Chinese spy.

The revelation Wednesday of a second extramarital affair , this time with an Nvidia employee reporting to Huang directly, added to the pressure, and another affair came to light later on Thursday after Huang’s ouster.

The scandal has implications far beyond one company: Huang’s central role in the AI race can’t be overstated. It was his vision of an AI future that led him to pivot Nvidia from a small company making video game chips into the dominant player in making the chips that serve OpenAI , Anthropic, and Google’s computing needs.

Huang is close friends with President Donald Trump’s and a leading voice in resisting efforts to slow AI progress. And he has pushed for the US to take a less hawkish position toward China’s own AI goals , a stance now called into question by his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Among its other impacts, the news has revived efforts on Capitol Hill to further restrict chip exports to China .

To break down the national security implications of Huang’s departure, how the Trump administration is involved, and what it says about US AI industry writ large, Today, Explained co-host Sean Rameswaram spoke with Garret De Vynck , a technology reporter at the Washington Post.

Below is an excerpt of their conversation, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get your podcasts, including Apple Podcasts , Pandora , and Spotify .

Nvidia has been called the central bank of AI, which is why it’s so important that we figure out what Jensen Huang may have disclosed to this alleged spy. How long has the president known about this, as far as we know?

As far as we know, the president has known about the fact that Jensen Huang was in a relationship with someone that the US government thought was a spy for about a year . This circulated within the administration, and the decision was made not to tell Jensen.

That doesn’t necessarily mean that it was automatically some kind of corrupt decision of President Trump protecting Jensen Huang. There’s all sorts of reasons why you might not want to tell someone they’re being spied on, the number one being that they might blow up the operation. Maybe you want to learn more. Maybe you suspect that the person themselves knows that they’re being spied on and is willingly sharing information and you need some more time to gather that. It’s unclear why the US government specifically chose not to pull in Jensen Huang.

It’s also a little bit unclear whether he knows he was being spied on, or whether maybe he was told through some kind of back channel. He has said that he did not know that she was a spy and he is admitting to the affair, to the infidelity. He’s admitting to essentially breaking Nvidia’s code of conduct by sleeping with one of its customers, but he is not admitting at all to knowing that she was a spy and definitely not admitting to sharing any information willfully.

It feels like this is the kind of thing that the government would investigate. There’s been reporting that the Commerce Department was involved with some kind of investigation, but that investigation came to an end and no one really knows why.

The context here is that the United States and China are in an AI race . Going back to the first Trump administration, there’s been pretty aggressive export controls saying, “We don’t want China to get our tech so that they can develop AI.” And the Biden administration continued that. He increased the export controls on China. China was complaining very loudly about this. They said, ‘We don’t care. We want to win AI and we need to slow you guys down.’

When Trump came in, he actually lifted his foot off the gas a little bit. They didn’t throw the gates open and say, “You can have whatever you want. All American companies can sell whatever they want to China.” But he said, “Some AI chips that are less powerful than the state of the art. We can send those to Chinese companies.“

The other thing that national security experts have pointed out is that the Trump administration could theoretically have been doing more to stop the smuggling of computer chips to China . And that’s where this story gets so important for national security.

Megaspeed is accused of essentially being a front for Chinese companies to get access to computer chips. Journalists have gone to Megaspeed’s office in Singapore where it’s based, and there were only a couple of people working there . It didn’t really seem like there was a lot going on. Nvidia has said all through this process over the last couple of years that, “No, we’ve checked it out, Megaspeed is a legitimate company and we’re not breaking the law when it comes to this.”

There are a lot of questions and what everyone is focused on finding out, both journalists and I would say congressional Democrats when they come into office in the new year is, is there something more going on here? Is there something where the Chinese either convinced Jensen Huang to sell more chips to them or Jensen Huang himself, who has been advocating for selling more chips to China, essentially did this himself?
“I think there’s this real question of: Do we see a much stronger push to actually ramp up controls on China and how does Trump respond?”

He’s been pressuring the president, he’s been donating to him , he’s been glad-handing with the president and the president has been listening more to this corporate executive who is his friend and who donated him a bunch of money rather than listening to China hawks or national security experts who say we should be limiting what China is able to access.

That’s really where the locus of this investigation is going to be. It’s not so much that Jensen Huang had an affair. It’s more the fact that he himself is someone who has said we need to sell more computer chips to China and he was involved with an alleged Chinese spy, and he’s very close to the president and had influence on the president.
You mentioned the Democrats. Have they said anything? Are they going to call him in front of Congress for an investigation?

Going forward, there are two big things here. One of them is these investigations into Jensen Huang and this whole situation. The company is likely going to continue to investigate. Maybe more information will come out there. Jensen Huang has been called to speak later this month in Congress. And congressional Democrats have also said that when they come into power in January, they will be asking him.

The second big thing that comes out of this is, what does America do when it comes to China and AI? Now that one of the biggest advocates for being a bit more friendly towards China when it comes to selling them things that they need for AI is out of the room and completely discredited, I think that the China hawks, those who say we need to crack down more aggressively, we need to limit China’s access to AI computer chips, they’re really coming into ascendance here and they’re in the Republican Party, they’re in the Democratic Party, some of them, people like Marco Rubio , are even in the Cabinet.

I think there’s this real question of: Do we see a much stronger push to actually ramp up controls on China and how does Trump respond? There’s all sorts of geopolitical things that could sort of spin out of this CEO affair.

I’m old enough to remember when a board tried to get rid of Sam Altman and then he was just back a week later . Elon Musk is already offering Jensen Huang a job . Is there a fair chance that he just goes somewhere that’s not that concerned about espionage affairs or getting with your VP of health or whatever it is? Is he just going to go work for China?

I don’t think he’s going to go work for China. This is definitely the wildest corporate story since Sam Altman was fired as CEO and brought back three or four days later. It’s a very different situation. That was a startup where you essentially have five or six investors who get to make the call about who the CEO is, and the employees at that company overwhelmingly wanted to bring Sam Altman back. I think they wanted more continuity of the company, but they also wanted to make sure that their company didn’t go under and go bankrupt and get disappeared, which was sort of on the table at that point in time.

Nvidia’s not going anywhere. Obviously employees have lost a lot of money in terms of the stock value already coming down due to the situation. So employees are probably shocked. They’re probably upset. Jensen Huang is broadly loved at Nvidia , and so I can definitely see that employees would be doing petitions, asking for him to return.

But this is a giant public company and the board makes a decision here. Jensen Huang was untruthful publicly and I think that also will make other public companies hesitant before rushing to bring him on as CEO.

As we’ve talked about many times in the show, half of our economy is staked on AI at this point. How concerned should we be that one of the most important people in this industry was so easily duped in this honeypot situation? Are these the people we should be trusting with the future of our society?

It’s a really good reminder that people are people. I think that we like to lionize individuals and say that they are the ones who are going to take us into the future and they are inventing the future and it’s so incredible. And I do think Jensen Huang gets a lot of credit for making sure that the companies kept up in AI, but at the end of the day, it was also a lucky break for them that the computer chips they were making just happened to work well for the math that is required by artificial intelligence.

I do think that this speaks to something that a lot of people across the country and maybe even the world really feel. They do not want to sign off the future to a dozen dudes in Silicon Valley and their collaborators in the Trump White House. I think that is a view that a lot of people increasingly have. I think it was one of the factors in the midterms, maybe not the most important one, but people are concerned about concentration of power. They’re concerned about AI and they don’t see it as something that they themselves have control over.

I think that this is just going to be another thing that sort of adds skepticism to the idea that people like Jensen Huang should be the ones making the final decision when it comes to artificial intelligence.

articles.headline: Slay the Spire 2's "biggest" beta patch yet adds its first new early access and foolish character, two game modes, and more tweaks than you can shake a stick at
keyFacts: Mega Crit released the biggest beta patch yet for Slay the Spire 2, adding new content that requires testing before hitting the main branch.
The update introduces a new early access character named The Fool, alongside two new game modes called Blitz and Dread.
Players can also experience various balance tweaks, including earlier rest sites, new events, and quality of life improvements.
body: Hark! A new Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch."

First up, a new character: The Fool! "Wah!! The first new character for Early Access arrives!" a Steam blog post explains. "A silly musician who wields a bow! How can such a whimsical creature survive within the Spire? Why, that's up to you! We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch. Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!" The post doesn't go into much detail as to what the new character can actually do, so, you'll have to discover that one for yourself!

There are also two new game modes to try out with this beta update. The first is Blitz, a "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode." Here, the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." You'll also find it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across every character, and you can unlock it by completing an Ascension run on any difficulty. The second mode is Dread, which as the name implies, is a "brutal" difficulty mode that you can only play if you've reached Ascension 10 on every character, including The Fool. "All ascension modifiers are enabled. Bosses are stronger and buff all enemies in their Act. Curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire. Death is expected."

You can expect a bunch of new balance tweaks and changes too. For starters, you'll find that rest sites can now appear a floor earlier every act. New events have been added to Underdocks and Act 2 and 3 too. Some nice quality of life alterations have been made, like how the character select screen for standard runs will start on whatever character you played as last, and controller navigation at the Merchant has been improved too. You can read all about the rest of the many changes right here.

articles.headline: New 4-minute Fable gameplay trailer shows a game that doesn't look much like Fable
keyFacts: Xbox released a four-minute gameplay trailer for the upcoming Fable reboot, which is scheduled to launch on February 23, 2027.
The trailer showcases combat, cinematics, and quests in a grim-looking setting, following the Hero of Briar Hill and Arden investigating magical issues.
Reddit users expressed mixed reactions, noting the game appears grim and conventional compared to previous bright entries in the Fable series.
body: The upcoming Fable reboot is set to launch on February 23, 2027, and with that date growing inexorably closer Xbox has dropped a new gameplay trailer showcasing four minutes of heroic questing across a rather grim-looking slice of Albion.
The trailer shows off a little bit of everything: some cinematics, some chitchat, the UI, and of course plenty of combat: melee, ranged, and even a bit of magic.
From the listing on YouTube:

"The Hero of Briar Hill has entered the depths of Deepwood alongside Arden, a local Hero, to investigate why strange magical happenings have been troubling the people of Oakshire. Here, they cross a threshold where the natural magic of Deepwood appears corrupted by an outside force, and they discover hints as to who or what could be responsible..."

The reaction to the video is quite positive among the YouTube comments but somewhat more subdued on the PC Gaming subreddit, where more than one poster suggested that it doesn't really show the game in its best light—which is to say that it doesn't really look like Fable, or at least what Fable fans expected. Fable 3 may not be everyone's favorite game in the series but it was bright, colorful, exuberant—this video, by comparison, seems downright grim and conventional.

That's about where I land on it: A four-minute clip obviously isn't going to tell the whole story, but with the video being showcased as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary, and the full Fable release now just three months away (unless it's delayed again), it's reasonable to assume that Playground and Xbox would want to put their best foot forward. And, well, this is fine, but I can't say it has me all charged up to play Fable: To me, it just feels kind of flat.
But maybe that's just me—we'll find out in February. Fable on the PC is available for pre-purchase now on Steam.

articles.headline: Democrats launch Nvidia investigation, write scathing letter on Huang’s ‘scheme’ with Trump
keyFacts: Congressional Democrats launched an inquiry on Thursday into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia chip sales to China.
Democrats wrote a letter questioning Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick regarding an alleged illegal revenue-sharing scheme and Nvidia donations to Trump projects.
Nvidia ousted CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday after he confessed to an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.
body: Democrats on Thursday opened an inquiry into how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China. Earlier on Thursday, the company ousted its CEO Jensen Huang. He also agreed to testify to a different set of Republican-led Congressional committees.

Huang was removed from the company he founded after he confessed to an extramarital affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. (He has since been accused of having more affairs, with Nvidia employees.)

The alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang, was an executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that U.S. officials suspect of helping route advanced Nvidia chips into China. The Democratic inquiry comes from Rep. Richard Neal (D-Mass.), the top Democrat on the House Ways and Means Committee, and Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), the top Democrat on the Senate Finance Committee. As the minority party, they can ask questions but can’t compel answers.
Their humdinger of a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asks the department to preserve records about an arrangement they find questionable and, they allege, illegal.

“The scheme worked like this,” as the letter describes it. President Trump agreed to sales of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China as long as the chips, manufactured by Taiwan, were first shipped to the United States. On arriving, Trump added a tariff “effectively taking a cut of Nvidia’s sales to China through what appears to be an unconstitutional export tax system,” the letter said. Then the Commerce Department, under Lutnick, issued an export license.

By the way, the deal between Trump and Nvidia to share revenue was public. In August 2025, Nvidia and AMD both agreed to share 15% of their revenue from chip sales to China with the U.S. government as part of a deal to secure export licenses, the AP reported at the time.

But the letter questions why Lutnick continued to allow Megaspeed to buy chips even after he was reportedly informed by U.S. intelligence of their suspicions of Alice Huang and of Jensen Huang’s relationship with her. It questions why the department reportedly green-lit other Asian companies to buy Nvidia chips “with no physical presence at their listed addresses.” So the inquiry is aimed at the administration, not just at Nvidia and Huang.

The letter also questions how Nvidia’s donations to Trump’s projects factored in. It notes that the export deal was approved after Trump learned of “Mr. Huang’s compromised position” in sleeping with an alleged spy, and after Nvidia donated $26 million toward Trump’s projects, including the ballroom. It appears to be asking if Trump used his knowledge of the affair to secure donations from Nvidia.

Interestingly, in a “60 Minutes” interview with President Trump that aired on Sunday, Trump mentioned how he and his team had threatened an unnamed AI exec with jail, and after that, the exec “totally changed.”

This Congressional investigation into Nvidia’s China sales and its dealings with Trump is the second one, so far, since news of the alleged spy affair broke. The Republican-led group involves leaders from the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the House Intelligence Committee. That group has demanded that Huang come to them and testify in a closed-door session. They had threatened to subpoena him if he didn’t voluntarily agree. On Thursday, after his resignation, he agreed.

articles.headline: Dozens of protesters arrested after staging sit-in at Chuck Schumer’s DC office
keyFacts: Dozens of protesters with the Sunrise Movement were arrested Thursday after staging a sit-in at Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer’s Washington office.
The protesters demanded that Senate Democrats prioritize ending the filibuster and replace Schumer with a leader who fights for young people.
The Sunrise Movement stated that Thursday’s action is one of several planned over the next two weeks targeting Senate Democrats.
body: Dozens of protesters with the Sunrise Movement, a youth climate organization, were arrested after staging a sit-in inside Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer’s Washington DC office Thursday

According to the Sunrise Movement, 54 people were arrested, among a few hundred who joined the protest from across the country, including some from New York, which Schumer represents. On its Instagram, the group is fundraising $24,000 to cover the bail fees and any potential legal fees for those arrested.
Capitol police were not immediately available for comment.

In a clip on the Sunrise Movement’s Instagram, with over 40,000 likes at the time of publication, young people sitting on the office floor chanted: “Hey hey, ho ho, Schumer has got to go!” Protesters, including children, held signs reading “The filibuster kills,” “Stop the climate crisis,” and “Schumer: Step up or step aside.”

As Senate Democrats prepare to vote on a majority leader for the upcoming Congress, they’re wrestling with how to navigate what feels like a clear mandate for anti-establishment voices from communities historically underrepresented in federal office to step into leadership. Several Democratic senators have said they will not support Schumer for the position, including Bernie Sanders, an independent who caucuses with the Democrats, as well as several members of the freshman class, like Michigan’s Abdul El-Sayed and South Carolina’s Annie Andrews.
Some have backed Maryland’s Chris Van Hollen as a challenger, including Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota’s senator-elect, and 50501, one of the major groups behind the No Kings protests.

The protesters on Thursday delivered a letter to Schumer arguing, per the group’s press release, that “after a collective decade of Schumer leadership it was time for change” and demanding Democrats prioritize ending the filibuster when Congress returns in January.

They also dropped the letters at the offices of every Senate Democrat. According to the Sunrise Movement’s campaigns director, Kidus Girma, Thursday’s action is one of several planned over the next two weeks targeting Senate Democrats and “demanding they actually take action”.

The group has regularly protested against politicians since first making headlines in 2018 with another sit-in targeting then-House speaker Nancy Pelosi, and helped launch calls for a Green New Deal alongside congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who was part of that 2018 sit-in. In the eight years since, Sunrise has supported progressive candidates, and last week, a Sunrise co-founder, Will Lawrence, 36, won his race for a Michigan US House seat after campaigning against datacenters.

“Young people went to Senator Chuck Schumer’s office to demand a Senate majority leader that would fight for the young people who elected a historic blue wave last week. They’re demanding change, not the same old, same old,” said Girma over the phone.

According to early data from Tufts University’s Center for Information and Research on Civic Learning and Engagement (Circle), which monitors youth civic engagement, the 3 November elections saw the second-highest youth turnout for a midterm election in 30 years – following only the 2018 midterms in Donald Trump’s first term.
“Chuck Schumer has been in office longer than I have been alive, and I’m 31 years old,” Girmus said. “[Young people] didn’t vote for a return to the Biden years, but rather a change.”

This isn’t the first sit-in of Schumer’s office organized by young people to happen this week. On Tuesday, three protesters were arrested during a protest by the youth advocacy group Get Free, who were there saying voters “need Democratic leaders to meet the moment lest we repeat history again”, according to executive director Nicole Carty.
Last week, Girma said the election outcome “shows that young people deeply, deeply care about their futures and the current government – but also, they’re making clear demands around how to fix it”.

articles.headline: Rep.-Elect Don Leonard Says Fellow Dems Threatened Him Over Hakeem Jeffries Vote
keyFacts: Rep.-elect Don Leonard stated that senior Democrats threatened him with political retaliation if he did not unconditionally support Hakeem Jeffries for House speaker.
Leonard said the threats included making his time in Washington difficult and ensuring he loses his election in two years.
Leonard conditioned his support for Jeffries on ending U.S. support for the war in Iran and Israel.
body: A newly elected House member who flipped a district seat blue in Ohio said he was threatened by senior Democrats if he didn’t unconditionally support Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (N.Y.) for House speaker.
Jeffries, now the minority leader, is the likely choice to succeed Rep. Mike Johnson (R-La.) after a blue midterm wave delivered the House and Senate to the Democrats.
But Rep.-elect Don Leonard (D-Ohio) didn’t appear to be feeling the collegial vibe this week during orientation on Capitol Hill.

Leonard said fellow lawmakers “told me in no uncertain terms that the decision as to whether or not I support Jeffries ... would basically mean both making my life a living hell for the next two years here in Washington as well as being sure to lose my election in two years.”

“It’s part of the stuff you see in the movies,” he continued in a clip shared by HuffPost alum Ryan Grim of Drop Site News. “It’s a whole other thing when, you know, when it’s in person by people who actually care about you and are cheering for you but expect you to wear the team jersey and be a good team player.”
Leonard said his conditions to back Jeffries included “ending U.S. support for the war in Iran and the country, Israel, that led us into it.”

“It was so much less cinematic. It was actually a dinner with senior elected officials, and I let them know where my position was on the speaker, and they were offering very friendly advice with very stark consequences,” Leonard said.
“Welcome to Washington, D.C., right? I’m not shocked, but I’m disappointed,” Leonard replied.
